Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#1
Main.sentence: The City College of the City University of New York (also known as the City College of New York , or simply City College or CCNY ) is a ___E:public U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university)___ ___E:research university U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_university)___ within the ___E:City University of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_University_of_New_York)___ (CUNY) system in ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#2
Main.sentence: Founded in 1847, City College was the first free public institution of higher education in the United States.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#3
Main.sentence: It is the oldest of CUNY's 25 institutions of higher learning  and is considered its flagship institution.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#4
Main.sentence: The main campus is located in the ___E:Hamilton Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton_Heights,_Manhattan)___ neighborhood.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#5
Main.sentence: City College's 35-acre (14 ha) campus spans Convent Avenue from 130th to 141st Streets.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#6
Main.sentence: It was initially designed by an architect ___E:George B. Post U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_B._Post)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#7
Main.sentence: City College's satellite campus, City College Downtown in the ___E:Cunard Building U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cunard_Building_(New_York_City))___ has been in operation since 1981, offering degree programs for working adults.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#8
Main.sentence: Among the precedents set by City College that helped shape the culture of American higher education are the following: the first student government in the nation (Academic Senate, 1867);  the first national fraternity to accept members without regard to religion, race, color or creed (Delta Sigma Phi, 1899);  the first degree-granting evening program (School of Education, 1907); and, with the objective of racially integrating the college dormitories, "the first general strike at a municipal institution of higher learning" led by students (1949).

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#9
Main.sentence: The college has a 48% graduation rate within six years.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#10
Main.sentence: It is ___E:classified U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnegie_Classification_of_Institutions_of_Higher_Education)___ among "R2: Doctoral Universities – High research activity."

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#11
Main.sentence: The City College of New York was founded as the Free Academy of the City of New York in 1847 by wealthy businessman and president of the Board of Education ___E:Townsend Harris U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Townsend_Harris)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#12
Main.sentence: A combination ___E:prep school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University-preparatory_school)___ , ___E:high school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_school)___ / ___E:secondary school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_school)___ and college, it would provide children of immigrants and the poor access to free higher education based on academic merit alone.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#13
Main.sentence: It was one of the early public high schools in the United States following earlier similar institutions being founded in ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_High_School_of_Boston)___ (1829), ___E:Philadelphia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_High_School_(Philadelphia))___ (1838), and ___E:Baltimore U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_City_College)___ (1839).

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#14
Main.sentence: The Free Academy was the first of what would become a system of municipally supported colleges – the second, ___E:Hunter College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hunter_College)___ , was founded as a women's institution in 1870; and the third, ___E:Brooklyn College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_College)___ , was established as a coeducational institution in 1930.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#15
Main.sentence: In 1847, New York State Governor ___E:John Young U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Young_(governor))___ had given permission to the state Board of Education to found the Free Academy, which was ratified in a statewide referendum.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#16
Main.sentence: Founder Townsend Harris proclaimed, "Open the doors to all… Let the children of the rich and the poor take their seats together and know of no distinction save that of industry, good conduct and intellect."

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#17
Main.sentence: ___E:Horace Webster U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horace_Webster)___ (1794–1871), a graduate of the ___E:United States Military Academy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy)___ at ___E:West Point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Point,_New_York)___ , was the first president of the Free Academy.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#18
Main.sentence: At the Free Academy's formal opening on January 21, 1849, Webster said:

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#19
Main.sentence: The experiment is to be tried, whether the children of the people, the children of the whole people, can be educated; and whether an institution of the highest grade, can be successfully controlled by the popular will, not by the privileged few.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#20
Main.sentence: In 1847, a curriculum was adopted that had nine main fields: mathematics, history, language, literature, drawing, natural philosophy, experimental philosophy, law, and political economy.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#21
Main.sentence: The academy's first graduation took place in 1853 in ___E:Niblo's Garden Theatre U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niblo%27s_Garden)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#22
Main.sentence: Even in its early years, the Free Academy had a framework of tolerance that extended beyond the admission of students from every social stratum.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#23
Main.sentence: In 1854, Columbia University denied distinguished chemist and scientist ___E:Oliver Wolcott Gibbs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Wolcott_Gibbs)___ a faculty position because of his ___E:Unitarian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unitarianism)___ religious beliefs.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#24
Main.sentence: Gibbs had been a professor at the Free Academy since 1848.  He later went on to an appointment at ___E:Harvard College U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#25
Main.sentence: In 1849 the prep school ___E:Townsend Harris Hall Prep School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Townsend_Harris_Hall_Prep_School)___ opened on campus, launched as a one-year preparatory school for CCNY.  In the early 1900s, as more Jewish students were enrolling, President ___E:John H. Finley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Huston_Finley)___ liberalized students' obligations by rescinding mandatory chapel attendance.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#26
Main.sentence: In 1866, the Free Academy, a men's institution, was renamed the College of the City of New York .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#27
Main.sentence: In 1929, the College of the City of New York became the City College of New York .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#28
Main.sentence: Finally, the institution became known as the City College of the City University of New York when the CUNY name was formally established as the umbrella institution for New York City's municipal-college system in 1961. The names City College of New York and City College, however, remain in general use.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#29
Main.sentence: With the name change in 1866, lavender was chosen as the college's color.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#30
Main.sentence: In 1867, the academic senate, the first student government in the nation, was formed.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#31
Main.sentence: Having struggled over the issue for ten years, in 1895, the ___E:New York State Legislature U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Legislature)___ voted to let the City College build a new campus.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#32
Main.sentence: A four-square block site was chosen, located at West ___E:Harlem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harlem)___ 's ___E:Manhattanville U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattanville,_Manhattan)___ , within the area which was enclosed by the ___E:North Campus Arches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org#North_Campus)___ ; the college, however, quickly expanded north of the Arches.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#33
Main.sentence: Like President Webster, the second president of the newly renamed City College was a ___E:West Point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy)___ graduate.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#34
Main.sentence: The second president, General ___E:Alexander S. Webb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_S._Webb)___ (1835–1911), assumed office in 1869, serving for almost the next three decades.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#35
Main.sentence: One of the ___E:Union Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Army)___ 's heroes at ___E:Gettysburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Gettysburg)___ , General Webb was the commander of the ___E:Philadelphia Brigade U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Brigade)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#36
Main.sentence: In 1891, while still president of the City College, he was awarded the ___E:Congressional Medal of Honor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medal_of_Honor)___ for heroism at Gettysburg.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#37
Main.sentence: A full-length statue of Webb, in full military uniform, stands in his honor at the heart of the campus.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#38
Main.sentence: The college's curriculum under Webster and Webb combined classical training in ___E:Latin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language)___ and ___E:Greek U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language)___ with more practical subjects like ___E:chemistry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemistry)___ , ___E:physics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physics)___ , and ___E:engineering U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engineering)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#39
Main.sentence: General Webb was succeeded by ___E:John Huston Finley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Huston_Finley)___ (1863–1940), as third president in 1903. Finley relaxed some of the West Point-like discipline that characterized the college, including compulsory religious chapel attendance.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#40
Main.sentence: ___E:Phi Sigma Kappa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Sigma_Kappa)___ placed its then-sixth chapter on the campus in 1896; alumni provided scholarships to new students entering the CCNY system for generations.  ___E:Delta Sigma Phi U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delta_Sigma_Phi)___ , founded at CCNY in 1899, claimed to be the first national organization of its type to accept members without regard to religion, race, color or creed.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#41
Main.sentence: Previously, fraternities at CCNY had excluded Jews.  The chapter flourished at the college until 1932 when it closed as a result of the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#42
Main.sentence: The founding of ___E:Zeta Beta Tau U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeta_Beta_Tau)___ at City College in 1898 was ___E:Richard Gottheil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Gottheil)___ 's initiative to establish a ___E:Jewish U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jewish)___ fraternity with ___E:Zionist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zionist)___ ideals.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#43
Main.sentence: It is now defunct.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#44
Main.sentence: Education courses were first offered in 1897 in response to a city law that prohibited the hiring of teachers who lacked a proper academic background.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#45
Main.sentence: The School of Education was established in 1921. The college newspaper, The Campus , published its first issue in 1907, and the first degree-granting evening session in the United States was started.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#46
Main.sentence: In the years when top-flight private schools were restricted to the children of the Protestant establishment, thousands of brilliant individuals (including Jewish students) attended City College because they had no other option.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#47
Main.sentence: CCNY's academic excellence and status as a working-class school earned it the titles " ___E:Harvard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University)___ of the ___E:Proletariat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proletariat)___ ", the "poor man's Harvard",  and "Harvard-on-the-Hudson."  ___E:Irving Howe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Howe)___ claims that when the Morris Cohen, the later philosopher, was a student at CCNY at the turn of the century, the faculty was "not very glittering" and the school was considered "at once grubby and exalted."

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#48
Main.sentence: Separate Schools of Business and Civic Administration and of Technology (Engineering) were established in 1919. Students were also required to sign a loyalty oath. In 1947, the college celebrated its centennial year, awarding honorary degrees to ___E:Bernard Baruch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Baruch)___ (class of 1889) and ___E:Robert F. Wagner U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Wagner)___ (class of 1898).

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#49
Main.sentence: A 100-year time capsule was buried in North Campus.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#50
Main.sentence: Until 1929, City College had been an all-male institution.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#51
Main.sentence: In 1930, CCNY admitted women for the first time, but only to graduate programs.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#52
Main.sentence: In 1951, the entire institution became coeducational.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#53
Main.sentence: Ten CCNY alumni who graduated in the mid 20th Century have since gone on to become ___E:Nobel Laureates U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Nobel_laureates_affiliated_with_the_City_University_of_New_York_as_alumni_or_faculty)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#54
Main.sentence: Many City College Alumni also served in the ___E:U.S. Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Armed_Forces)___ during the ___E:Second World War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_World_War)___ (1939/41–1945).

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#55
Main.sentence: A total of 310 CCNY alumni were killed in the War. Prior to World War II, a large number of City College alumni—relative to alumni of other U.S. colleges—volunteered to serve on the ___E:Republican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Spanish_Republic)___ side in the ___E:Spanish Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Civil_War)___ (1936–1939).

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#56
Main.sentence: Thirteen CCNY alumni were killed in Spain.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#57
Main.sentence: In its heyday of the 1930s through the 1950s, CCNY became known for its political ___E:radicalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radicalism_(historical))___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#58
Main.sentence: It was said that the old CCNY cafeteria in the basement of Shepard Hall, particularly in alcove 1, was the only place in the world where a fair debate between ___E:Trotskyists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trotskyism)___ and ___E:Stalinists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stalinism)___ could take place.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#59
Main.sentence: Being part of a political debate that began in the morning in alcove 1, ___E:Irving Howe U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving_Howe)___ reported that after some time had passed he would leave his place among the arguing students in order to attend class.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#60
Main.sentence: When he returned to the cafeteria late in the day, he would find that the same debate had continued but with an entirely different cast of students.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#61
Main.sentence: The municipality of New York was considerably more conformist than CCNY students and faculty.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#62
Main.sentence: The Philosophy Department, at the end of the 1939/40 academic year, invited the British mathematician and philosopher ___E:Bertrand Russell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bertrand_Russell)___ to become a professor at CCNY. Members of the ___E:Roman Catholic Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church)___ protested Russell's appointment.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#63
Main.sentence: A woman named Jean Kay ___E:filed suit against the state Board of Higher Education to block Russell's appointment U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bertrand_Russell_Case)___ on the grounds that his views on marriage and sex would adversely affect her daughter's virtue, although her daughter was not a CCNY student.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#64
Main.sentence: Russell wrote "a typical American witch-hunt was instituted against me."  Kay won the suit, but the board declined to appeal after considering the political pressure exerted.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#65
Main.sentence: Russell took revenge in the preface of the first edition of his book An Inquiry into Meaning and Truth , which was published by the Unwin Brothers in the United Kingdom (the preface was not included in the U.S. editions).

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#66
Main.sentence: In a long précis that detailed Russell's accomplishments including medals awarded by Columbia University and the Royal Society and faculty appointments at Oxford, Cambridge, UCLA, Harvard, the Sorbonne, Peking (the name used in that era), the LSE, Chicago, and so forth, Russell added, "Judicially pronounced unworthy to be Professor of Philosophy at the College of the City of New York."

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#67
Main.sentence: In 1945, the ___E:Knickerbocker Case U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knickerbocker_Case)___ was set off when William E. Knickerbocker, chairman of the ___E:romance languages U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_languages)___ department, was accused of ___E:antisemitism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antisemitism)___ by four faculty members.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#68
Main.sentence: They claimed that "for at least seven years they have been subjected to continual harassment and what looks very much like discrimination" by Knickerbocker.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#69
Main.sentence: Four years later, Knickerbocker was again accused of antisemitism, this time for denying honors to high-achieving Jewish students.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#70
Main.sentence: About the same time, William C. Davis of the economics department was accused by students of maintaining a racially segregated dormitory at Army Hall.   Davis was the dormitory's administrator.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#71
Main.sentence: CCNY students, many of whom were World War II veterans, launched a massive strike in 1949 in protest against Knickerbocker and Davis.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#72
Main.sentence: The New York Times called the event "the first general strike at a municipal institution of higher learning."

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#73
Main.sentence: As student radicalism increased in the late 1960s, with the ___E:Civil Rights Movement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Movement)___ and ___E:anti-Vietnam War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opposition_to_United_States_involvement_in_the_Vietnam_War)___ feelings increased, culminating at CCNY during a 1969 protest takeover of the South campus,  African American and ___E:Puerto Rican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rican_American)___ activists and their white allies demanded, among other policy changes, that the City College implement an aggressive ___E:affirmative action U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affirmative_action)___ program to increase minority enrollment and provide academic support.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#74
Main.sentence: At some point, campus protesters began referring to CCNY as "Harlem University." The administration of the City University at first balked at the demands, but instead, came up with an ___E:open admissions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_admissions)___ or open-access program under which any graduate of a New York City high school would be able to matriculate either at City College or another college in the CUNY system.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#75
Main.sentence: Beginning in 1970, the program opened doors to college to many who would not otherwise have been able to attend college.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#76
Main.sentence: The increased enrollment of students, regardless of college preparedness, however, affected City College's and the university's academic reputation and strained New York City's financial resources.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#77
Main.sentence: A 2023 documentary film directed by ___E:Greta Schiller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Schiller)___ and ___E:Andrea Weiss U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Weiss_(filmmaker))___ , The Five Demands , provides historical coverage and interviews with students who led the 1969 protests.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#78
Main.sentence: City College began charging tuition in 1976. By 1999, CUNY's board of trustees voted to eliminate remedial classes at CUNY's senior colleges, thereby eliminating a central pillar of the policy of open admissions and effectively ending it.  Students who could not meet the academic entrance requirements for CUNY's senior colleges had to enroll in the system's ___E:community colleges U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_college)___ , where they could prepare for an eventual transfer to one of the 4-year institutions.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#79
Main.sentence: Since this decision, all CUNY senior colleges, especially CCNY, have begun to rise in prestige nationally, as shown by school rankings and incoming freshman ___E:GPA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPA)___ and ___E:SAT U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAT)___ scores.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#80
Main.sentence: The end of open admissions led to a change in CUNY's student demographics, with the number of Black and Hispanic students decreasing and the number of White Caucasian and Asian students increasing.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#81
Main.sentence: As a result of the 1989 student protests and building takeovers in response to tuition increases, a community action center was opened on the campus, called the Guillermo Morales/Assata Shakur Community and Student Center, located in the NAC building.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#82
Main.sentence: The center was named after CUNY alumni ___E:Assata Shakur U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assata_Shakur)___ [note 1] and ___E:Guillermo Morales U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Guillermo_Morales&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , [note 2] both of whom ___E:self-exiled U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-exile)___ in ___E:Cuba U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuba)___ .

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#83
Main.sentence: Students and neighborhood residents who used the center for community organizing against issues of racism, police brutality, and the privatization and militarization of CUNY faced opposition from the City College administration for years.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#84
Main.sentence: After a long controversy, in October 2013, City College eventually shut down the Guillermo Morales/Assata Shakur Community and Student Center, citing a need for space to expand its career center; this closure provoked student demonstrations.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#85
Main.sentence: CCNY's new Frederick Douglass Debate Society defeated ___E:Harvard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard)___ and ___E:Yale U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale)___ at the "Super Bowl" of the ___E:American Parliamentary Debate Association U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Parliamentary_Debate_Association)___ in 1996. In 2003, the institution's ___E:Model UN U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Model_UN)___ Team was awarded as an Outstanding Delegation at the National Model United Nations (NMUN) Conference, an honor that it would repeat four years in a row.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#86
Main.sentence: The ___E:U.S. Postal Service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Postal_Service)___ issued a postcard commemorating CCNY's 150th anniversary, featuring Shepard Hall, on Charter Day, May 7, 1997.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#87
Main.sentence: The ___E:City University of New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_University_of_New_York)___ began recruiting students for the University Scholars program in the fall 2000, and admitted the first cohort of undergraduate scholars in the fall 2001. CCNY was one of five CUNY campuses, on which the program was initiated.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#88
Main.sentence: The newly admitted students became undergraduates in the newly formed Honors Program.

Main.id: City College of New York - Wikipedia#89
